clue.text: Indefinite number of Romans with malaria

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ague is an old name for malarial fever

explanation.surface: A vague count of how many Romans caught malaria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number of Romans' points to a Roman numeral, here V for five.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague is unclear or imprecise, so it is indefinite.

clue.text: Drawing pole on a sailing boat

parts.note: S stands for the south pole
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A picture of a mast standing on a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the pole S above, so before, the boat; 'pole' looks like a mast but is the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing.

clue.text: Bathes in befuddling alcoholic drink

indicators.note: befuddling means confusing or muddling, so the letters of the two words before it are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone takes a bath in a drink that leaves them fuddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befuddling' rearranges the eight letters of BATHES and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green spirit flavoured with wormwood.

clue.text: Wherein young scions are raised

parts.note: reads like a place where heirs of noble families grow up, but scions are also young shoots of plants, raised in a garden centre of seedlings

explanation.surface: Where the children of a great house are brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is both a children's room and a place where young plants are grown.

clue.text: Unfavourable view that stopped play?

explanation.surface: A dim outlook that brought the game to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, umpires stop play when the light is too poor for batters to see the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To be seen 'in a poor light' is to be viewed unfavourably, and gloomy conditions halt a cricket match.

clue.text: Maybe only a sneeze, though it usually requires a choke

definitions.text: Maybe only a sneeze, though it usually requires a choke

parts.words: Maybe only a sneeze, though it usually requires a choke
parts.note: the first sign of catching a chill may be a sneeze, while an old car engine fired up from chilly needs the choke pulled out

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a sneeze that nonetheless leaves them choking.
explanation.walkthrough: A choke is a valve on older petrol engines that richens the fuel mix when the engine has not warmed up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the beginning of an illness of the nose and also firing up an engine from chilly.

clue.text: Lecture on gossip

parts.note: a lecture is a talk
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A lecture given on the subject of tittle-tattle.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss others idly is to gossip about them.

clue.text: Dry wine?

parts.note: asks for a wine that is typically dry, a white from a Burgundy town

explanation.surface: Asking for a glass of something that is not sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Mâcon is a town in southern Burgundy whose white wines are typically dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a Burgundy wine, its whites usually dry.

clue.text: Irish house put up AD one fifty

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are written bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A house in Ireland built in the year 151 AD.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns only AD; then I and L follow as Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dáil is the lower chamber of the Irish parliament.

clue.text: Cuts short dog-ends

explanation.surface: Someone trims the stubs of cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: A cur is a mongrel dog, so its tails are its ends; 'dog-ends' is British slang for cigarette butts.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail something is to cut it short, and a cur's tails are literally dog ends.

clue.text: Refer to everybody with due formality

parts.note: everybody means all

indicators.note: a loose signal: going through the formality rearranges the word due into a new order

explanation.surface: Addressing everyone with proper ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formality' is a very loose anagram signal, turning DUE into UDE after ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude to something is to mention it indirectly, to refer to it.

clue.text: Western headgear calling for identification

parts.note: a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: A cowboy hat that asks to be identified.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation asks someone to say which thing or which one, seeking identification.

clue.text: Put down theology lessons by church emissary

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
a legate is a papal envoy

explanation.surface: Religious lessons delivered by the Pope's representative are dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to demote or move to a lower rank.

clue.text: Bloomer occurred when an uppercut found its mark

definitions.text: Bloomer occurred when an uppercut found its mark

parts.words: Bloomer occurred when an uppercut found its mark
parts.note: an uppercut lifts the boxer's jaw, so the jaw went up; the words also describe a flowering shrub

explanation.surface: A boxer made a blunder when his uppercut landed.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as CHIN AROSE, the jaw went up after the punch; read whole it is a hibiscus, the bloomer.
explanation.definitionFit: The China rose is a flowering hibiscus shrub, so a bloomer.

clue.text: Egg-beater which disappears after a close shave

definitions.text: which disappears after a close shave

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget and a near miss with a razor.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisk-er beats eggs, and a hair on the face is gone after shaving.

clue.text: Drink offered for sale, and delivered

parts.note: to sup is to drink
plied means sold, as a trader plies wares

explanation.surface: A drink was offered for sale and handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplied goods have been provided or delivered.

clue.text: Man's conservative record of the past

parts.note: his means belonging to a man
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician's track record.
explanation.definitionFit: History is the account of past events.

clue.text: Having taken the cloth according to customers requirements

explanation.surface: A priest made to measure for the buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: To take holy orders, or 'the cloth', is to become a priest; a tailor also works to customers' orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordained clergy are in holy orders, and goods made to order follow buyers' instructions.

clue.text: Antiques which former enemies should let be

definitions.text: which former enemies should let be

explanation.surface: Old relics that reconciled foes should leave alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says to let bygones be bygones: forget past grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: Old household items are collected as relics of the past, and the proverb urges forgetting past quarrels.

clue.text: Where the rice planter is very angry

explanation.surface: A farmer working the rice fields in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: A paddy is a flooded rice field and, in British slang, a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice grows in flooded paddy fields, and a paddy is also a temper tantrum.

clue.text: Latest TV aerial for serving up soap?

explanation.surface: The newest satellite receiver for showing TV serials.
explanation.walkthrough: A soap opera is served up on a satellite dish, and a bar of soap sits in a soap dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite dish receives television, and a dish is a plate or bowl for holding things.

clue.text: All right, ring Catherine

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
Kay is a short form of the name Catherine

explanation.surface: Agreeing to telephone a woman called Catherine.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection means acceptable or agreed.

clue.text: Get down request from one frightened of the dark

definitions.text: request from one frightened of the dark

explanation.surface: A scared child asking to be lifted down.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A LIGHT, it is what a child afraid of darkness asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to dismount or step off, and asking for a lamp is a plea from someone scared of night.

clue.text: Miss Lind used to spin yarns

explanation.surface: A singer who used to tell tall tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny Lind was a famous Swedish soprano; the spinning jenny was an early multi-spindle machine for spinning thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lind's first name, and a frame of the Industrial Revolution for spinning cotton thread.

clue.text: Gathers tempting extras on offer

explanation.surface: Someone collects the special deals on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: In dressmaking, gathers are pleated strips of fabric, like ruffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffled trims are gathered strips of cloth, and unnecessary perks are optional extras.

clue.text: Hour-glass for one who is gettingon

explanation.surface: An elderly person contemplating an egg-timer.
explanation.walkthrough: An hourglass is literally an old-fashioned timer; the slang term also means a veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand glass is an ancient timing device, and the phrase is slang for an elderly person.

clue.text: He leads her to you and me

definitions.text: He leads her to you and me

indicators.note: to means added onto the end of, so this piece is attached after the other

parts.note: you and me together are us
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man shows a woman over to where we are sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' puts HER after US; the whole clue is also what an usher does.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats, leading them to the others.

clue.text: Negative earthing which almost proved fatal

parts.note: N is short for negative
taken as written

explanation.surface: Faulty electrical grounding that nearly killed someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negative' and 'earthing' sound electrical, but N is just the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A close call is an escape that barely avoided disaster.
